outcome: Preeclampsia with severe features or eclampsia
cohort: The study included 7,955,713 pregnancies from all live and stillbirths recorded in linked vital statistics and hospitalization discharge data across California (2008-2018), Michigan (2008-2020), Oregon (2008-2020), Pennsylvania (2008-2014), and South Carolina (2008-2020).
finding: Chronic hypertension was associated with a substantial fraction of adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes, including preeclampsia with severe features or eclampsia, acute renal failure, and pulmonary edema, and contributed to higher complication rates, particularly for Black or Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander individuals, despite similar risk ratios across racial-ethnic groups.
